ALERT_REPEAT_INTERVAL.description: How often an ongoing failure is notified again (`6h`, `2d`); `0` never repeats (ADR 33).

APPRISE_NOTIFY_ON.description: NOTIFY_ON for Apprise alone. One of `failures`, `problems`, `everything`.

APPRISE_TAGS.description: The Apprise tag for each kind, such as `failure=critical,problem=alerts,routine=quiet`; a kind left out goes to `all`.

APPRISE_URL.description: Secret: put it in a file (apprise_url in the secrets directory, or name the file in APPRISE_URL_FILE), never an environment variable.

BACKUP_PARALLELISM.description: How many services a backup processes at once, each with its hooks and backup. 1 backs them up one after another.

BACKUP_SCHEDULE.description: When backups run, as a cron expression (`0 3 * * *`). Unset: manual mode, nothing is scheduled.

CHECKIN_URL.description: A dead man's switch pinged after each backup run (ADR 37): Uptime Kuma push URLs get `status=up`/`down`, others `/fail` on failure.

CHECK_BACKUPS.description: Whether maintenance checks the storages. Turn off on a deployment sharing a storage another one maintains.

CHECK_INTERVAL.description: How often each secondary is checked (`12h`, `7d`); a target's own STORAGE_TARGET_N_CHECK_INTERVAL wins. Default: a day, a week for SFTP-like storages.

DELETE_EXTRA.description: auto-restore: delete files the revision does not have.

DRY_RUN.description: auto-restore: show what would be restored, replaced and deleted, and restore nothing.

DUPLICACY_THREADS.description: Threads each Duplicacy backup, copy, check and restore uses.

HASH_COMPARE.description: auto-restore: compare files by content, not size and time.

HOOKS_DIR.description: Hooks come from `<HOOKS_DIR>/<service>/` instead of the service directories (ADR 45).

HOSTNAME.description: Overrides the host part of snapshot IDs and the kit's name. Keep it stable: changing it starts new snapshots.

IGNORE_OWNERSHIP.description: auto-restore: leave ownership alone (without CHOWN and FOWNER it is left anyway, with a warning).

LOG_FORMAT.description: `json` writes the container's output as one JSON object per line. One of `text`, `json`.

MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULE.description: When storage check and prune run. Unset: they run only on `archiver maintenance`.

METRICS_PORT.description: Serves Prometheus metrics on `/metrics` there (ADR 35); `logs/archiver.prom` is written either way.

NOTIFICATION_SERVICE.description: `Pushover` sends to Pushover with the secrets below (any letter case). One of `Pushover`, `None`.

NOTIFY_ON.description: Which notifications every destination receives (ADR 36). One of `failures`, `problems`, `everything`.

NO_PREVIEW.description: restore: skip the preview of what an interactive restore changes.

NTFY_NOTIFY_ON.description: NOTIFY_ON for ntfy alone. One of `failures`, `problems`, `everything`.

NTFY_TOKEN.description: Secret: put it in a file (ntfy_token in the secrets directory, or name the file in NTFY_TOKEN_FILE), never an environment variable.

NTFY_URL.description: An ntfy server and topic, such as `https://ntfy.sh/my-archiver`.

PRUNE_BACKUPS.description: Whether maintenance prunes by PRUNE_KEEP. Turn off on a deployment sharing a storage another one maintains.

PRUNE_EXHAUSTIVE_FREQUENCY.description: How often the prune also removes chunks no revision references. One of `off`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`.

PRUNE_KEEP.description: Duplicacy retention: one revision a day for a week, a week for a month, a month for half a year, none older.

PUSHOVER_API_TOKEN.description: Secret: put it in a file (pushover_api_token in the secrets directory, or name the file in PUSHOVER_API_TOKEN_FILE), never an environment variable.

PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_ON.description: NOTIFY_ON for Pushover alone. One of `failures`, `problems`, `everything`.

PUSHOVER_USER_KEY.description: Secret: put it in a file (pushover_user_key in the secrets directory, or name the file in PUSHOVER_USER_KEY_FILE), never an environment variable.

RECOVERY_KIT_EXTRA_PATHS.description: Files or directories also carried in the kit's `extra/`, separated by colons.

RECOVERY_PASSWORD.description: Secret: put it in a file (recovery_password in the secrets directory, or name the file in RECOVERY_PASSWORD_FILE), never an environment variable.

RECOVERY_PASSWORD_FILE.description: recover: a file holding the kit's password, instead of the prompt.

RESTORE_DRILL_DIR.description: Scratch space a drill restores into and deletes afterwards; never a service directory.

RESTORE_DRILL_EXCLUDE.description: Services drills leave out, separated by commas.

RESTORE_DRILL_SCHEDULE.description: When restore drills run (ADR 28). Unset: no drills.

RESTORE_DRILL_SERVICES.description: How many services each drill restores from each storage, rotating; `all` restores every one.

RESTORE_DRILL_STORAGES.description: Which storages drills restore from: `all`, `primary`, or storage names separated by commas.

RESTORE_PATHS.description: auto-restore: only these paths in the snapshot, separated by commas.

RESTORE_THREADS.description: auto-restore: threads for this restore. Default: DUPLICACY_THREADS.

ROTATE_BACKUPS.description: Old name of PRUNE_BACKUPS, still read when PRUNE_BACKUPS is unset.

RSA_PASSPHRASE.description: Secret: put it in a file (rsa_passphrase in the secrets directory, or name the file in RSA_PASSPHRASE_FILE), never an environment variable.

RSA_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.description: The RSA private key to place in the container's key directory at start.

RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE.description: The RSA public key to place at start.

RUN_RESTORE_SERVICE.description: auto-restore: run the service's post-restore hook after the files are restored.

SECRETS_DIR.description: Where secret files are read from. Any secret can instead be named by `<SECRET>_FILE`.

SERVICE_DIRECTORIES.description: Directories to back up, separated by colons or newlines; each may be a bash glob such as `/srv/*/`. Each directory is one snapshot, `<hostname>-<directory name>`.

SSH_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.description: SFTP storages: the SSH private key to place at start.

SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE.description: SFTP storages: the SSH public key to place at start.

STORAGE_PASSWORD.description: Secret: put it in a file (storage_password in the secrets directory, or name the file in STORAGE_PASSWORD_FILE), never an environment variable.

STORAGE_TARGET.description: auto-restore: restore from this storage (name or number) only.

TZ.description: Time zone for schedules and log timestamps, such as `America/New_York`.

WEB_PORT.description: Serves the read-only status page there (ADR 38). It has no login: put it behind an authenticating proxy.
